subject: humanities
passage: In the painting workshop maintained by the Mughal emperor Akbar in the late sixteenth century, an illustrated manuscript page was seldom the work of a single artist from start to finish. ______ the labor was usually divided among specialists: one painter sketched the overall composition, a second applied the colors, and a third, often a celebrated portraitist, painted the faces of the principal figures. Brief notes written in the margins of many surviving pages record which artist performed each of these tasks.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The first sentence says what usually did not happen: one artist doing a whole page. The second sentence says what happened in its place: the work was divided among specialists. A transition that introduces an alternative to something just ruled out is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The division of labor is not a result of pages seldom being one artist's work; it is the same practice described positively.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Moreover" adds a new point, but the second sentence does not add a separate idea; it states what replaced single-artist work.
explanation.C: Correct. "Instead" signals that dividing the labor among specialists took the place of a single artist finishing the page.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean the division of labor happened in spite of the first sentence, but the two sentences agree: a page was seldom one artist's work because the labor was shared. This is the closest near miss because it is also a contrast word.
